linked_tweets.author: Gergely Orosz
linked_tweets.content_zh:
当生成代码变得便宜而验证它是困难的部分时，软件工程会是什么样子？一个罕见的播客，关注与构建软件相关的一切，由@satyanadella 主持。 时间戳：

24:06 为什么采用 AI 与采用 React 不同
26:29 软件工程师角色的变化
29:25 微软的自愿退出要约
34:05 AI焦虑和角色转变
36:35 初级招聘
42:36 开放模特
45:39 拥有你的人工智能基础设施
51:21 建立对人工智能代理的信任
53:48 本地模型和混合智能
56:39 微软的模型策略
59:26 给工程师的建议
1:01:21 结束要点

为您带来：

• @turbopuffer – 基于对象存储构建的矢量和全文搜索引擎。它快速、便宜且可扩展性极强。 （我用它构建了一个大大改进的播客/新闻搜索，请查看：）

• @ Linear – 团队和代理的产品开发系统。

• @WorkOS – 让您的应用程序为企业做好准备所需的一切。

Satya 的 3 个有趣要点：

1. 一种新的软件工程形式：团队构建软件工厂来改进他们的工作。

Satya 引用了 Azure 网络团队的例子，该团队管理着 500 多家光纤网络运营商，并且最近构建了一个代理系统来更好地管理电子邮件和流程。现在，他们的运营效率大大提高了。 Satya 认为这是“人工智能转型”的现实：棕地致力于建设软件工厂，以改善团队的运作方式，同时继续日常工作。

2.“拥有情报”：避免锁定并将代理视为内部风险。

Satya 警告公司要避免与任何单一模型提供商锁定，确保线束、内存和模型不耦合，以便可以轻松更改。他还认为更多的公司应该考虑使用开放模型来保护其核心知识产权（IP）免遭泄露，并建立私人评估来决定使用和升级到哪些模型。他还表示，模型是智能的，但不可靠，因此最好将它们视为“内部风险”，并构建一个单独的系统来验证代理系统是否按预期工作。

3. 这些自愿退出要约是怎么回事？

我直接问萨提亚，为什么微软最近向大多数软件工程师提出了自愿退出的提议，这在公司历史上还是第一次。我还想知道这是否意味着将来会裁员。不出所料，他的回答很外交，但在播客中我以更直接的方式重申了我听到的内容。
linked_tweets.content_en:
What does software engineering look like when generating the code becomes cheap and verifying it is the hard part? A rare podcast focused on everything around building software, with @satyanadella.  Timestamps:

00:00 Intro
02:12 Microsoft’s open-source shift
04:15 Building VS Code in the open
05:55 Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code
09:52 Decision engines
12:32 Verifying AI-generated code
15:39 The software factory
20:45 Bringing AI to existing products
24:06 Why adopting AI is different to adopting React
26:29 The changing role of software engineers
29:25 Microsoft’s voluntary exit offers
34:05 AI anxiety and changing roles
36:35 Junior hiring
42:36 Open models
45:39 Owning your AI infrastructure
51:21 Building trust in AI agents
53:48 Local models and hybrid intelligence
56:39 Microsoft’s model strategy
59:26 Advice for engineers
1:01:21 Closing takeaways

Brought to you by:

• @turbopuffer  – a vector and full-text search engine built on object storage. It’s fast, cheap, and extremely scalable. https://t.co/w9y67Gs8ab (I built a greatly improved podcast/newseltter search with it, check it out: https://t.co/6zbxlEaHlu)

• @linear  – the product development system for teams and agents. https://t.co/knIF2mcz9p

• @WorkOS  – everything you need to make your app enterprise-ready. https://t.co/aiAee0oF5h

3 interesting takeaways from Satya:

1. A new form of software engineering: teams building software factories to improve their work. 

Satya cites the Azure networking team which manages 500+ fiber network operators and recently built an agentic system to better manage emails and processes. Now, they operate much more efficiently as a result. Satya sees this as the reality of “AI transformation”: brownfield work on building software factories to improve how teams operate, all while continuing the day-to-day work.

2. “Own the intelligence”: avoid lock-in & treat agents as an insider risk. 

Satya cautions companies to avoid lock-in with any single model provider by ensuring that the harness, memory, and model are not coupled, so that they can be changed with ease. He also thinks more companies should consider using open models as a way to protect their core intellectual property (IP) from leaking out, and build private evals to decide what models to use and upgrade to. He also says that models are intelligent but unreliable, so it’s best to treat them as “insider risks” and build a separate system to verify that agentic systems work as expected.

3. What’s with those voluntary exit offers? 

I asked Satya directly why Microsoft recently made voluntary exit offers to most of its software engineers for the first time in the company’s history. I also wanted to know if it could mean layoffs in the future. Unsurprisingly, his reply was diplomatic, but in the podcast I rehashed what I heard in a more direct way.

linked_tweets.author: RaArΞs ⚓️
linked_tweets.content_zh:
公司在人工智能上花费了数百万美元，期望生产力爆炸式增长

但哈佛大学的一项新研究发现了一些完全不同的东西

这项研究在 5 年内跟踪了 718 家公司和大约 3 亿个数据点。

研究结果有点有趣。

采用人工智能编码工具后，开发人员：

i) 多编写 30% 的代码行

ii) 多提交 20% 的代码

iii) 增加 23% 的拉取请求

听起来生产力正在飞速增长，对吗？

除了已完成的项目和已完成的 Jira 任务几乎没有变化...AF 怎么样？

▫️ 显然，编写代码所节省的时间都花在了其他地方。

Pull 请求的批准时间延长了 49%，
审稿人多留下了 35% 的评论
审查期间需要更改的代码加倍

说得通。

人工智能可以在几分钟内生成数千行，但仍然需要有人审查、测试和批准它们。

甚至提到亚马逊的服务中断与人工智能辅助代码有关，此后该公司引入了更严格的人工审查。

▫️ 编码之外的事情也是一样的。

> 使用人工智能抄写员的医生节省了写笔记的时间，但花更多的时间来完成这些笔记。

> 律师事务所因虚假人工智能引文而面临处罚，而德勤则不得不部分退还包含类似问题的政府报告。

▫️ 与此同时，公司已经以人工智能效率的名义进行裁员。

美国运通宣布裁员 5%，为人工智能做准备，而微软则向 6 万名员工提供自愿离职方案。

哈佛大学的研究发现几乎没有证据表明更快的编码可以转化为更多成品软件或需要更少的员工......

我的意思是，vibe 编码很棒，但开发工作尚未完成......

有些人仍然需要审查，修复错误，测试所有内容，并确保它不会破坏其他东西......

我认为开发人员我们会安全一段时间
linked_tweets.content_en:
companies are spending millions on AI, expecting productivity to explode

but a new Harvard study found something quite different 👇

this sstudy tracked 718 companies & around 300m data points over 5 years.

the findings are kinda interesting.

after adopting AI coding tools, devs were:

i) writing 30% more lines of code

ii) committing 20% more code

iii) opening 23% more pull requests

sounds like productivity is going through the roof, right?

except completed projects & finished Jira tasks BARELY CHANGED... HOW THE AF? 

▫️ apparently, the time saved writing code went somewhere else.

pull requests took 49% longer to approve, 
reviewers left 35% more comments 
& code needing changes during review doubled

makes sense tbh.

AI can generate 1000s of lines in minutes, but someone still needs to review, test & approve them.

there is even a mention of Amazon outage linked to AI-assisted code, after which the company introduced stricter human reviews.

▫️ same thing outside coding.

> doctors using AI scribes saved time writing notes, but spent more of their patient visits finishing those notes.

> law firms faced penalties over fake AI citations, while Deloitte had to partially refund a government report containing similar problems.

▫️ meanwhile, companies are already cutting jobs in the name of AI efficiency.

American Express announced 5% workforce cuts to prepare for AI, while Microsoft offered voluntary exit packages to 60,000 workers.

and the Harvard study found little evidence that faster coding translated into more finished software or fewer employees needed...

i mean, vibe coding is great, but devs work isn't done yet... 

someomne still needs to review, fix the mistakes, test everything, and make sure it doesn't break something else...

i think devs we'll be safe for a while
